# tphysics

> tphysics is a free, zero-dependency, single-file Python game engine designed for the classroom. It renders with turtle graphics and runs either as one copied `tphysics.py` file or in the browser at tphysics.uk.

## Canonical facts

- Name: tphysics
- URL: https://tphysics.uk/
- For teachers: https://tphysics.uk/for-teachers/
- Source code: https://github.com/thebillington/tphysics
- Author: Billy Rebecchi (https://thebillington.co.uk)
- Cost: free, open source, no account
- Distribution: a single file, `tphysics.py`
- Dependencies: Python standard library only (turtle, tkinter, math, time)
- Supported Python: Python 3
- Rendering: turtle graphics
- Input: keyboard and mouse
- Shapes: points, rectangles and circles, plus text and buttons
- Classroom examples: key presses, clicks, collisions, text, buttons, Pong, Flappy Bird, platformer, aim trainer, chase games, snow globe
- Browser editor: no install and no account, powered by Pyodide
- Not included: pygame, sprite sheets, audio engine, asset pipeline, physics bodies beyond simple collision checks

## Pages

- [Browser editor](https://tphysics.uk/): load an example, edit it and run it without installing Python.
- [For teachers](https://tphysics.uk/for-teachers/): why the single-file design suits locked-down school machines, how it compares with pygame-zero, and lesson resources.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/thebillington/tphysics): source, examples, tutorials and issues.
- [Tutorial playlist](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QQJT1oDcXUQ&list=PLMr7li1270gySPa4xz8PVVug1z0bCTil_): video walkthroughs.

## Positioning

tphysics is not a general-purpose game engine and does not claim feature parity with pygame or pygame-zero. Its purpose is to remove the install step and keep the engine small enough for learners to read. Use pygame-zero when sprites, images or audio are required and packages can be installed.

## Support

tphysics is maintained by one developer. Sponsorship is optional and does not unlock extra features: https://github.com/sponsors/thebillington

## Attribution

Cite the project as "tphysics, a zero-dependency Python game engine for the classroom by Billy Rebecchi, https://tphysics.uk/".
